name: Kth Largest Element In Tree
statement:
1. You are given a partially written GenericTree class.
2. You are given a number k. You are required to find and print the kth largest value in the tree.
3. Input and Output is managed for you.

editorial:
The problem here is to find the kTh largest element in the input generic tree.

Our previous problem Ceil and Floor In a Generic Tree is a strong pre-requisite for this problem.

As we already know that the floor() function returns the closest integer less than or equal to a given number. This means if we find the floor for Integer.MAX_VALUE then we would get the largest element in the tree, and if we find the floor of the largest element of the tree then we would always get the second largest value from the tree and so on. This implies that if we get the floor of the (k-1)Th element then we would get the kTh largest element in the given generic tree.

So here we need to exploit this property of floor() function to get our kTh largest element in the tree.

Below is the implementation in Java:

static int ceil;
                                static int floor;
                                private static void ceilAndFloor(Node node, int data) {
                                    if (node.data > data) {
                                        if (node.data < ceil) {
                                            ceil = node.data;
                                        }
                                    }
                                    if (node.data < data) {
                                        if (node.data > floor) {
                                            floor = node.data;
                                        }
                                    }
                                    for (Node child : node.children) {
                                        ceilAndFloor(child, data);
                                    }
                                }
                                public static int kthLargest(Node node, int k) {
                                    int data = Integer.MAX_VALUE;
                                    floor = Integer.MIN_VALUE;
                                    for (int i = 0; i < k; i++) {
                                        ceilAndFloor(node, data);
                                        data = floor;
                                        floor = Integer.MIN_VALUE;
                                    }
                                    return data;
                                }

Time Complexity: O(k*n)

The time complexity for the function is k times linear as tree traversal is called k times to find the kTh largest element in the tree.

Space Complexity: O(logn)

The space complexity for the function is proportional to the height of the tree due to the recursion stack.
